narration.allowedTopic: thanking the child for repairing the harbor bridge
narration.fallbackText: You fixed my bridge! Every crew in the bay walks across it now. Thank you, friend.

dialogue.text: You fixed my bridge! Every crew in the bay walks across it now. Thank you, friend.
Good to see you again. The bridge is still broken. Would you help me count the planks?
Ahoy! I am Pip, and this is my shipyard. There is always something to build here.

choices.label: That sounds like a big job!

dialogue.text: The bridge to the cove lost half its planks in the last storm. I need someone good at counting to help me build it back.

questOffers.summary: Help Pip count and measure planks to repair the harbor bridge.

npcs.role: Shipyard foreman at Pirate Builder Bay. Offers the bridge repair quest.

choices.label: It was a lot of fun!

dialogue.text: The Great Storybook is whole again, and every page remembers you. Thank you, my friend.
The story you made is on my shelf now. Shall we start a new one?
Oh dear. The Great Storybook was torn, and its pages flew all over the castle. Will you help me bring them back?

narration.allowedTopic: welcoming the child into the castle library full of unfinished stories
narration.fallbackText: Welcome to the castle library. Every story here is missing one thing: your ideas.

dialogue.text: Welcome to the castle library. Every story here is missing one thing: your ideas.

questOffers.summary: Build a story with Keeper Quill, one choice at a time.
The Great Storybook lost its pages. Help Keeper Quill bring them back.
The Great Storybook lost its pages. Find them and bring them back to Keeper Quill.
Pages of the Great Storybook are scattered through the castle. Find them all and restore the book.

npcs.role: Storykeeper Castle librarian. Invites children to build a story together.

dialogue.text: My favorite helper is back. I saved the interesting gears for you.

narration.allowedTopic: introducing a cluttered workshop full of springs and gears
narration.fallbackText: Careful where you step, there are springs everywhere. I am Bolt. I fix things.

dialogue.text: Careful where you step, there are springs everywhere. I am Bolt. I fix things.

questOffers.summary: Help Bolt sort the workshop parts into the right bins.

npcs.role: Tinkerer at Bolt's Workshop. Offers building and sorting work.

narration.allowedTopic: a dragon delighted that the sanctuary forge is burning again
narration.fallbackText: Look at it! Warm all the way to the back wall. I had almost stopped believing it would light again. Thank you.

dialogue.text: Look at it! Warm all the way to the back wall. I had almost stopped believing it would light again. Thank you.

choices.label: I will go and set them.

narration.allowedTopic: a dragon urging the child to set three found runes into the forge hearth
narration.fallbackText: All three! You found all three. Take them to the hearth and set them in the sockets. I would do it myself, but my claws are far too big for the little slots.

dialogue.text: All three! You found all three. Take them to the hearth and set them in the sockets. I would do it myself, but my claws are far too big for the little slots.

narration.allowedTopic: a dragon describing where three fire runes came to rest around the valley
narration.fallbackText: Three fire runes, and they are not lost so much as scattered. One rolled behind the Keeper Lodge. One is down among the boulders. And one is out on the cold ledge where you can see the sky cliffs.

dialogue.text: Three fire runes, and they are not lost so much as scattered. One rolled behind the Keeper Lodge. One is down among the boulders. And one is out on the cold ledge where you can see the sky cliffs.
You are the one who helped me. I remember. This sanctuary is yours to visit anytime.

narration.allowedTopic: a dragon explaining that the sanctuary forge went out and needs three missing runes
narration.fallbackText: The forge went out. That is what happened. Everything here ran on its warmth, and when it stopped, the hatchery went cold and the others left one by one. I cannot light it. It needs its three fire runes, and I cannot find them.

dialogue.text: The forge went out. That is what happened. Everything here ran on its warmth, and when it stopped, the hatchery went cold and the others left one by one. I cannot light it. It needs its three fire runes, and I cannot find them.

npcs.role: Young dragon at the Dragon's Sanctuary. Appears only after the Ember Mountain story, and asks the child to help relight the forge.

narration.allowedTopic: thanking the child for relighting the harbor lighthouse
narration.fallbackText: You got the old lamp turning! Ships have been coming in all morning. I will not forget it.

dialogue.text: You got the old lamp turning! Ships have been coming in all morning. I will not forget it.

narration.allowedTopic: asking the child for help restarting the lighthouse machine
narration.fallbackText: I cannot open the gate while the lighthouse is dark. Would you take a look at the machine?

dialogue.text: I cannot open the gate while the lighthouse is dark. It would not be safe. The machine inside stopped, and I am no good with machines. Would you take a look?

narration.allowedTopic: welcoming the child to a harbor town whose machines have stopped
narration.fallbackText: Welcome to Clockwork Harbor. It is quieter than it should be. Half the town has stopped ticking.

dialogue.text: Welcome to Clockwork Harbor. It is quieter than it should be, I am afraid. Half the town has stopped ticking.

narration.allowedTopic: explaining that the harbor gate stays shut while the lighthouse is dark
narration.fallbackText: The lighthouse stopped. No light, no safe way in, so the gate stays shut and the ships wait.

dialogue.text: The lighthouse stopped, is what happened. No light, no safe way in, so the gate stays shut and the ships wait out there in the dark. The machine that turns it is inside, and it is beyond me.

questOffers.summary: Help the Harbor Master get the lighthouse turning again.

npcs.role: Keeper of the harbor gate at Clockwork Harbor. Offers the lighthouse repair quest.

narration.allowedTopic: hinting that something older beneath the harbor is still failing
narration.fallbackText: The lamp is turning! But that is not the real trouble. Something older, further down, is running badly.

dialogue.text: The lamp is turning! Good. But listen - that is not the real trouble. Something much older, much further down, is running badly. Can you hear it?

narration.allowedTopic: an inventor puzzling over harbor machinery that has started failing
narration.fallbackText: Gears, gears, gears. Everything here runs on them, and lately they run backward, or not at all.

dialogue.text: Gears, gears, gears. Everything here runs on them, and lately they run backward, or not at all. I have three notebooks full of it and no answer yet.

npcs.role: Inventor at Clockwork Harbor. Explains how the harbor machinery works.

dialogue.text: You did it, explorer! The volcano is calmer, and the first Heart Crystal fragment is safe with us.
Is that glow what I think it is? Show me the crystal fragment!
Hello, explorer! I am Professor Ember. I study volcanoes, and this one has started to rumble.
Deep below us there is hot melted rock called magma. When it moves, the ground shakes and steam comes out.
Look through my telescope. Can you find the crater, the lava, and the steam?
Firepeak is waking up! Look through my telescope and find three clues: the crater, the lava flow, and a steam vent.
You found all three! Now let us go look closer.
Great observing! The steam and lava tell us magma is moving. Let us cross the lava river and look closer.
Scientists watch volcanoes from a safe distance with telescopes and cameras.
Fill each gap with the stone that fits. The glowing outline shows the size.
The old stone bridge fell into the lava. Each gap needs a stone exactly as long as the gap. Look at the gaps and choose wisely.
The crossing is safe now. Walk across the stones!
Basalt is a dark rock that forms when lava cools quickly.
Turn the valves to send the steam out of the passage and up into the sky.
Hot steam is blocking the passage. Each valve moves steam from one pipe to another. Follow the steam to the sky vent.
Whoosh! The steam goes up the sky vent and the passage opens.
Steam is water heated until it turns into a gas. It pushes hard when it is trapped.
Something is glowing on the old pedestal. Go and look!
Crystals grow slowly as hot rock cools. This one also glows with island magic.
Real crystals grow when hot, mineral-rich liquid cools slowly and its tiny parts line up in a pattern. This one also glows with island magic.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: Take it back to Professor Ember. The rope lift will carry you.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: Show Professor Ember the crystal fragment.
Thank you, explorer! You have earned the Volcano Explorer Badge. There are more crystal secrets deeper in the mountain, for another day.

questOffers.summary: Help Professor Ember find out why Firepeak is waking up.

npcs.role: Volcano researcher at Firepeak base camp. Offers The Volcano Awakens.

dialogue.text: You did it, explorer! The Heart of Firepeak is glowing and the mountain is calm. I could not have done it without you.
You read the map very well. Follow the path north to Emberwood Forest. Kindle is waiting there.
Welcome, explorer! I heard you helped Professor Ember wake Firepeak safely. Now the mountain needs a hero for its Heart.
Welcome to Firepeak, explorer! I am Flint. The Heart of the mountain has gone dim, and I could use your help.

The Heart of Firepeak is a crystal of island magic. It keeps the mountain calm. Seven places lie ahead, and each one has a puzzle that brings a little of its light back. Take your time, there is no rush.
Walk with the controls, and press jump to hop over small things. Every jump has a path you can walk instead, so you never have to jump. If you fall, you will start again from the last checkpoint.
Good luck, explorer! I will be right here if you want to talk.
This is my map of Firepeak. Tap three places on it and I will tell you about each one.
This is my map of Firepeak. Find five places on it: the forest, the lava river, the caverns, the forge and the summit. Take your time.
You found three places! Now we know where we are going.
You found all five places. A good explorer reads the map before the journey. The forest gate is open.
Scientists who study volcanoes use maps to see where the mountain is high, where the lava flowed, and where it is safe to walk.

questOffers.summary: Help Flint light the Heart of Firepeak again.

npcs.role: Explorer and guide at Explorer’s Landing. Offers The Heart of Firepeak.

dialogue.text: The Heart is glowing and the mountain is calm! I am a little spark of island magic, and I am glad I got to explore with you.
The Heart is shining! Go and tell Ignis. I will wait right here.
All four crystals are in place. Now we can set the shard back into the Heart.
You crossed the lava river! I like warm places, but even I stay on the bridge.
You counted the embers! The path ahead leads to the lava river. Stay on the bridge and the stones.
Hello! I am Kindle, a little fire spirit made of island magic. May I come along on your adventure?
I carry the crystals and I like to give hints. When a puzzle is tricky, ask me, and I will help you think about it. You always do the solving.
Look closely at the puzzle and say the question out loud. Try one answer. If it is not right, you can try again as many times as you like.
See you soon! I will stay close.
These crystals make a pattern. Look closely. What comes next?
Patterns grow and change. Study the crystals and the numbers, then work out what comes next.
Yes! You spotted the pattern. Well done!
You found the rule of the pattern. Rules help us know what comes next, even before we see it.
I collected some embers. Can you count them with me?
My embers are sitting in groups. Count in steps, or count the groups, to find how many there are.
You counted them just right. The path through the forest is open!
Counting in groups is quicker than counting one by one. The forest path is open!
Each stone has a number. Choose the stone that makes the sum true, and a bridge will rise.
The stones across the lava river are numbered. Solve the sum or the fact, and choose the stone with the answer. A wide bridge will rise.
The bridge is rising. You can walk across!
The bridge is ready. If you like a challenge, the stepping stones lead to a hidden shard.
Two paths, two numbers. Which number is bigger, or which is smaller?
Each path shows a number or a fraction. Compare them, and choose the path the puzzle asks for.
That is the right path. Off we go to the caverns!
Comparing carefully, you chose well. The way to the caverns is open.
The four crystals are in place. Now let us set the shard back into the Heart together.
Look! The Heart is glowing again. Go and tell Ignis!

npcs.role: A small, friendly fire spirit made of island magic. Gives hints and carries crystals.

dialogue.text: The Heart glows and the mountain is calm. Remember, real volcanoes are watched carefully by scientists. You made a fine scientist today.
You reached the top, and you named the rocks. Ignis is waiting just beyond the summit.
You know your rocks. Next, a story about how volcano islands grow. It is real science.
The cavern is lit. The crystals here glow because of island magic. The rocks around them are real volcanic rock.

choices.label: Can you give me a hint?

dialogue.text: Greetings, young scientist! I am Professor Basalt. I study real volcanoes. Some things on Firepeak are island magic, and I will tell you which is which.

choices.label: Can you give me a hint?

dialogue.text: Real volcanoes have hot melted rock called magma underground. When it comes out, it is called lava, and it cools into rock. The glowing crystals and the Heart of Firepeak are island magic.
Scientists look carefully and compare. Look at the clues in the puzzle, think about each answer, and try the one that fits best.
Keep asking questions, scientist. That is how we learn.
The crystals in here are shaped like circles, squares, triangles and hexagons. Match each one to its clue.
Crystals can have many faces, sides and corners. Read the clue carefully, then pick the shape that fits it.
You know your shapes! The crystals glow brighter.
Well matched. Counting sides and corners is how mathematicians tell shapes apart.
Put the crystals in a row, from the smallest to the largest.
Put the crystals in order. Follow the rule on the card: it may be the number of sides, or the size of a fraction.
A perfect row! The cavern is lit.
The order is right and the cavern is lit. A secret passage has opened too.
Real crystals grow slowly, over a very long time, inside rock. These ones also glow with island magic.
In the real world, crystals grow when minerals in hot liquid cool slowly and their tiny parts line up in a pattern. The glow in this cave is island magic, not science.
Here are rock samples from the mountain. Let us learn about them. Choose the answer you think is right.
Here are three rocks from Firepeak: basalt, pumice and obsidian. Look at how each one looks and feels, then answer.
Well done, young scientist!
Excellent! You are thinking like a volcano scientist.
Real volcanoes have hot melted rock called magma underground. When it comes out, it is called lava. Lava cools and hardens into rock.

Basalt, pumice and obsidian are igneous rocks: they form when lava cools. Basalt is dark and heavy. Pumice is full of tiny bubbles and so light that it can float. Obsidian is shiny volcanic glass. A volcano is active if it can erupt, dormant if it is sleeping, and extinct if it is not expected to erupt again.
Real islands can be made by volcanoes! Put the steps in order to see how.
Some real islands were built by volcanoes. Put the steps in order, from the magma deep below to the island above the sea.
You told the story of a volcano island in the right order!
That is the true story of a volcanic island. The summit is yours to explore. Ignis is waiting beyond.
Magma rises, lava comes out and cools into rock, and over a very long time the rock piles up into an island.

In the real world, magma rises and erupts under the sea. Lava cools into new rock, and layer upon layer builds up over a very long time, until the volcano rises above the water. The island of Hawaii grew this way.

npcs.role: Volcano scientist. Explains how real volcanoes, rocks and islands work.

dialogue.text: The forge hums and the Heart glows. Thank you, friend. I will keep the machines in good order.
The forge is working again, and the steam gates are open. Go up to the summit. The view is grand.
Hear that hum? The machine is powered. One more puzzle, and the lamp will shine.
Ah, a visitor. I am Cinder. I keep the old forge, but the machines have been quiet for a long time. Could you help me wake them?
Every machine works in steps. One thing happens, then the next. If you do the steps in the right order, the machine runs. Go slowly and think it through.
Ask yourself what must happen first. Then ask what comes next. Say the steps out loud, one at a time.
Take your time. The forge will wait.
The old machine needs three switches pressed in the right order. Think about what must happen first.
The machine needs four steps in the right order. Remember: before the gears turn, the water must cool. Read the clues, then press the switches.
It hums! You got the order just right.
The forge is powered. Machines work when each step happens in the right order.
The lamp needs power. Which path reaches the lamp?
A circuit must make a full path for the power to flow. Find the path that completes the circuit, or share the crystals fairly if the clue asks.
The lamp is shining! The steam is clearing.
The circuit is complete and the forge is restored. The steam gates are open.
In real life, electricity flows only when there is a complete loop, called a circuit. A gap in the loop stops it.

npcs.role: Keeper of the Ancient Forge. Needs help restarting the old machines.

dialogue.text: The Heart of Firepeak shines and the mountain is calm. You brought the light back. The island thanks you, explorer.
We did it. The whole mountain is warm and calm. Take the portal back to the landing whenever you like.
The Heart is glowing, thanks to you. Come and tell me what it was like.
The four crystals are in their places. Kindle will help you set the shard into the Heart.
You came a long way to reach me. The Heart is dim, and four crystals came with you. Will you set them in order?
Welcome, traveler. I am Ignis, the guardian of the Heart. The way to the Heart opens when you have crossed the whole mountain.
The Heart is a crystal of island magic. When we set the crystals in the order of your journey, it remembers the places you passed through, and it glows. There is no hurry.
Think back to your journey. Which place came first? Which came next? Say them in order, then set the crystals.
Go gently, explorer. The mountain is glad you came.
Four crystals came with you on your journey. Set them in the order you found them.
Read the clues about your journey. Then set the four crystals in the order you found them.
You remembered the whole journey. Thank you!
You set them in the order of your journey. The Heart has begun to glow.
The Heart is shining again. Come and tell me all about it.
The mountain is calm again. Thank you, brave explorer!
The mountain is calm and the Heart glows. Thank you, explorer, for your patience and your clear thinking.

npcs.role: Gentle guardian of the Heart of Firepeak. Asks the child to set the crystals in order.
